proposal.body:
<!--
CHANGELOG.md is generated from merged pull requests. Do not add an entry unless this PR introduces
a deprecation or breaking change.
-->

Camel tests currently force span-kind suppression instead of exercising the production default. This change makes the default task use semconv suppression while preserving focused coverage of span-kind behavior.

- **Suppression coverage:** Correct mode detection for an unset strategy and the current property. The dedicated `testSpanKindBasedSuppression` task uses:
  ```text
  -Dotel.instrumentation.common.span-suppression-strategy=span-kind
  ```
- **Test variants:** Remove redundant semconv overrides and task; rename the independent messaging, classpath, and disablement variants.
- **Metadata collection:** Update Camel task selection and metadata configuration for the distinct variants.

<!-- START COPILOT CODING AGENT SUFFIX -->



<!-- START COPILOT ORIGINAL PROMPT -->



<details>

<summary>Original prompt</summary>

> User request: "send this to copilot cloud coding agent to impl and open the PR"
> 
> Implement a Camel-only test/build alignment in open-telemetry/opentelemetry-java-instrumentation and open a separate draft pull request against main. Leave PR #20471 and its head branch unchanged. Do not modify Couchbase or Redisson. Do not change production Camel telemetry or rewrite its HTTP decorators.
> 
> Confirmed scope:
> - Make Camel's ordinary test task use the production-default semconv-based span suppression. Remove the blanket span-kind override in instrumentation/camel-2.20/javaagent/build.gradle.kts and unnecessary explicit semconv overrides.
> - Remove the redundant base testStableSemconv/testSemconv task once test covers the same configuration. Keep the existing independent messaging, dependency/classpath, experimental, and v3-preview coverage.
> - Rename the remaining stale testStableSemconv*/testSemconv* variants to describe their actual independent setting. Suggested names are testReceiveTelemetry, testJmsDisabled, testSjmsWithoutCamelJms, testCamelDisabled, and testAdaptersDisabled.
> - Preserve deliberate coverage of the supported span-kind strategy in an explicitly named testSpanKindBasedSuppression task. Use the stable property otel.instrumentation.common.span-suppression-strategy for explicit strategy configuration. Keep genuinely strategy-sensitive coverage; avoid redundant unrelated test matrices.
> - Correct SuppressionTest's mode detection so an absent property means semconv, not span-kind, and it recognizes the strategy property actually used by the tasks. Preserve the correct nested-HTTP span assertions for both modes. Update other test expectations only as required by this test-configuration change.
> - Update check dependencies, metadataConfig/collectMetadata wiring where applicable, and the Camel entries in .github/scripts/instrumentations.sh. Ensure metadata collection continues to exercise the relevant distinct telemetry variants without stale task names or redundant default-mode execution.
> 
> Investigation already completed:
> - PR #5779, commit 4e3f19d4692075bd98dfb86326f2575b99caa02c, made span-key/semconv suppression the global default in April 2022. It added Camel's span-kind test override as a workaround, with a TODO to use semantic attribute extractors. The author's explanation is at https://github.com/open-telemetry/opentelemetry-java-instrumentation/pull/5779#discussion_r850419308.
> - PR #19483, commit 267f78730769927a940ffda6acba232520860884, introduced messaging-specific extractors and explicit semconv overrides for Camel's stable-messaging/v3-preview variants. Non-messaging components were unchanged.
> - PR #20382, commit 307d34fb06c0f384c78f4a696844cce364c3c1cd, removed messaging selector settings but retained the suppression differences and stale task names.
> - CamelSingletons uses a generic decorator-based AttributesExtractor for non-messaging HTTP spans. It does not claim the HTTP client span key. The nested HTTP-client span is therefore emitted under semconv suppression and suppressed under span-kind. RestCamelTest, SingleServiceCamelTest, and TwoServicesWithDirectClientCamelTest already use SuppressionTest to assert these differences.
> - SuppressionTest currently decides whether to expect the nested HTTP-client span by comparing the deprecated property directly to "semconv". This incorrectly interprets an absent setting as span-kind.
> - Only Camel and RocketMQ 4.8 currently set the suppression strategy in instrumentation build scripts. RocketMQ leaves default tests alone and selects span-kind only in a narrowly filtered testBatchSendSuppression variant. The repository's usual pattern is default behavior in test and separately named JVM variants for non-default features, not a semconv-selection name for suppression.
> 
> Follow repository instructions and its PR template. Apply targeted formatting and validate the Camel test variants, including ordinary test, explicit span-kind coverage, and affected messaging variants. Keep the change confined to test/build alignment and directly related metadata/documentation wiring. Open the draft PR after implementation and describe that tests now use the production default while preserving explicit legacy-strategy coverage. If validation is blocked, state the exact blocker rather than claiming it passed.


</details>
proposal.title: Align Camel tests with default span suppression
